verdict.rationale: Smithery is a SaaS MCP registry and connection platform that handles user data and credentials, so a training-data opt-out is a fair privacy-posture question for it. Nothing in the evidence pack mentions an AI-training opt-out, a data-usage policy, or any commitment not to train on user data. Encrypted credential storage and scoped service tokens are adjacent security controls, not training-use protections, so they earn no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models
